invariant: Preserve and present truth through evidence; do not classify administrations or policies as better/worse.
scope_note: This batch adds independent policy nodes. It is not an administration-completeness claim. Economic/industrial activity changes remain primary inventory when federally governed and environmentally operative.

nodes.exact_title: Safe Drinking Water Act Amendments of 1986
operative_mechanisms: created an aquifer-protection demonstration program
required state-developed critical wellhead protection programs
required development of drinking-water standards for additional contaminants
strengthened EPA enforcement involving public water systems and underground injection well operators

nodes.exact_title: Superfund Amendments and Reauthorization Act of 1986
operative_mechanisms: amended CERCLA
increased emphasis on permanent remedies and treatment technologies
expanded enforcement and settlement authorities
increased state and public participation
increased focus on human-health risks from hazardous-waste sites
expanded Superfund financing

nodes.exact_title: Emergency Planning and Community Right-to-Know Act of 1986 (SARA Title III)
operative_mechanisms: state and local chemical-emergency planning structure
hazardous chemical inventory and emergency release reporting
community right-to-know access
Toxics Release Inventory under section 313
acid-rain control program
expanded controls for urban air pollution and toxic air emissions
ozone-depleting chemical phaseout provisions
national operating permits program
strengthened enforcement
established national policy prioritizing pollution prevention/reduction at source where feasible
directed EPA to establish a source-reduction program
provided for information collection/dissemination and state technical-assistance grants
expressly linked pollution prevention to changes in industrial production, operation, and raw-material use
nodes.scope_significance: Demonstrates why industrial/economic activity cannot be relegated to a later control when the policy itself operates through industrial processes.

nodes.exact_title: Bottled Water Standard of Identity / Quality recodification and definitions
operative_mechanisms: recodified bottled-water quality standards at 21 CFR 165.110
revised bottled-water definition to include mineral water with specified exceptions and ingredient uses
defined artesian, ground, mineral, purified, sparkling bottled, spring, sterile, and well water
made source-category claims such as spring water subject to regulatory definitions
nodes.source_status: official_FDA; final-rule Federal Register citation/native text still to be custodied

nodes.exact_title: Bottled Water Quality Standard amendment for chemical contaminants
operative_mechanisms: established or revised allowable levels for 13 chemicals in the bottled-water quality standard
nodes.source_status: official_FDA inspection/regulatory history; Federal Register/native rule still to be custodied
